Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Quinton de Kock gets a guard of honor from his fellow teammates. David Warner and Mitchell Marsh are the openers for Australia will the latter on strike. Lungi Ngidi comes to bowl. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The Aussies were really good for the first half of the innings. The likes of Ellis, Nesser, Abbott, and Zampa kept things under control and also got wickets. However, in the second half of the innings, they let the hosts off the hook. The fielding wasn't the best and the bowling was also a little off. They now face a stiff task as the wicket does have something in it for the bowlers. They though have batters in form. South Africa will know if they bowl well, this is well and truly dependable. Join us for the chase in a bit.

That's a strong total posted by South Africa on a wicket that has seemed tough to bat on for most parts of the innings. Also, after being 4 down for not a lot, South Africa will be pleased with their recovery. Markram and Miller's stand is what got their innings back on track. Markram was the highlight with the bat. He missed out on a ton by just 7 runs. Miller too played well but fell at the wrong time. Jansen though played a brilliant cameo and Andile too did an excellent job with the bat to take their side over 300 run mark at the end!
FOUR! What a finish from Andile Phehlukwayo! Touch short and on off, Andile Phehlukwayo picks it well and slaps it over extra covers for a boundary. South Africa end their innings for 315/9!

Commentary.Commentary: Right then, we are done with the pre-match proceedings. The players take their respective field positions. Out come the two South African batters - Temba Bavuma and Quinton de Kock. The latter has announced his retirement after the World Cup so this will be his last home game. Michael Neser has the new ball in hand. Let's play...

We are all set for the Super Sunday. It is bright and sunny, perfect weather for a full game of cricket. The players stride out in the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Australia's first followed by the national anthem of South Africa.

PITCH REPORT - Pommie Mbangwa is pitchside. He says that there is a bit of grass and it's a beautiful surface. He says that as it's an early start it's a tacky surface but it will improve and turn into a belter.

Temba Bavuma the skipper of South Africa says that they would have bowled as well. Says that putting runs on the board is never bad and they will be bold in this game as well. He adds that they will look to give a complete performance in this game as well and ends by mentioning the changes on their side.

Mitchell Marsh the skipper of Australia says that they will bowl first. Adds that the start is a bit early so it can be a tricky wicket. He says that its a good day and they will look to win the series and the message before the game was to trust their plans. Ends by mentioning the changes.

Australia (Playing XI) - David Warner, Mitchell Marsh (C), Josh Inglis (In for Marcus Stoinis), Marnus Labuschagne, Alex Carey (WK), Cameron Green (In for Travis Head), Tim David, Sean Abbott (In for Josh Hazlewood), Michael Neser, Nathan Ellis, Adam Zampa.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock (WK), Temba Bavuma (C) (In for Reeza Hendricks), Rassie van der Dussen, Aiden Markram, Heinrich Klaasen, David Miller, Marco Jansen, Andile Phehlukwayo (In for Kagiso Rabada), Gerald Coetzee, Keshav Maharaj, Lungi Ngidi.
TOSS - Australia have won the toss and will BOWL first.

Well, Australia will be disappointed with their efforts in the previous two games. Their batters flumped in their previous couple of games as well losing the game by a 100-plus runs margin. Their bowlers failed to deliver as well and they will look to rectify the mistakes and win this ODI series. Also, Travis Head's injury can be a big concern for the side as they head into the World Cup. Which side will come out on top? Stay tuned to find out. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

So, after losing the T20I series by 3-0, the Proteas lost the opening two games of the ODI series as well, and that too by a huge margin. Well, they then bounced back in some style, winning the next two games comprehensively courtesy of blistering tons from Aiden Markram and Heinrich Klaasen in 3rd and 4th ODI respectively and some top-level bowling bowling display. They will now look to win this series with the ODI World Cup around the corner.

A very warm welcome, folks! It is time for the fifth and the decider game of the Australia tour of South Africa. The series has witnessed some exciting events so far as it stands 2-2 as of now. Both sides here will look to win the game and the series as they head towards the mega event in India. So, who will win? Stay tuned to find out, as this game promises to be a cracker...
